name: OPERA
aliases: Overactive Bladder: Performance of Extended Release Agents
question: How do once-daily extended-release oxybutynin and tolterodine compare for urge urinary incontinence in women with overactive bladder?

design.population: Women with overactive bladder, 21–60 urge urinary incontinence episodes weekly, and at least 10 voids per 24 hours.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Patients and Methods; Results

verdictNote: Primary urge incontinence reductions were similar; frequency and complete continence favored oxybutynin.
takeaway: In women with overactive bladder, oxybutynin ER and tolterodine ER produced similar reductions in weekly urge incontinence over 12 weeks; oxybutynin reduced voiding frequency more and yielded more women without incontinence, with more dry mouth.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed: June 2003; day not specified
reports.citation: Diokno AC, Appell RA, Sand PK, et al. "Prospective, randomized, double-blind study of the efficacy and tolerability of the extended-release formulations of oxybutynin and tolterodine for overactive bladder: results of the OPERA trial." *Mayo Clin Proc.* 2003;78(6):687-695. doi:10.4065/78.6.687

results.measure: Change in weekly urge urinary incontinence episodes through 12 weeks
results.note: The abstract calls the improvements similar but gives no effect estimate, confidence interval, or prespecified testing threshold.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Patients and Methods; Results

results.measure: Reduction in voids per 24 hours through 12 weeks

values.exp: greater reduction; numeric change not stated
values.ctl: smaller reduction; numeric change not stated

results.measure: Efficacy-assessed women reporting no urinary incontinence episodes in their last 7-day voiding diary
results.note: Absolute risk difference in percentage points, calculated from the reported rounded percentages; the abstract does not state event numerators.

harms.label: Dry mouth
harms.note: Usually mild; P=0.02. A later OPERA analysis reports rates and a different P value.

harms.label: Discontinuation due to adverse events
harms.note: Rates are not stated in the primary abstract.

delivery.label: Treatment and diary schedule
delivery.value: Oxybutynin ER 10 mg or tolterodine ER 4 mg daily for 12 weeks; 24-hour urinary diaries at baseline and weeks 2, 4, 8, and 12.

reports.label: CNS tolerability analysis
reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed: June 2005; day not specified
reports.citation: Chu FM, Dmochowski RR, Lama DJ, et al. "Extended-release formulations of oxybutynin and tolterodine exhibit similar central nervous system tolerability profiles: a subanalysis of data from the OPERA trial." *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2005;192(6):1849-1854. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2005.03.036

harms.label: Reported central nervous system adverse events
harms.note: No significant between-group difference; events were mild or moderate. No serious treatment-related adverse events were reported in either group.
